steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Consumer Rights Act 2015 is the main law protecting consumers. It applies to goods, services, and digital content purchased in the UK.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Three key rights for goods: they must be as described (match their description), fit for purpose (do what the buyer reasonably expects), and of satisfactory quality (meet the standard a reasonable person would accept).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: If goods are faulty: within 30 days — full refund; after 30 days but within 6 months — repair or replacement (retailer chooses); if repair/replacement fails — refund (with deduction for use after 6 months).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Services must be performed with reasonable care and skill, at a reasonable price, and within a reasonable time. If not, the consumer is entitled to a repeat performance or price reduction.

steps.title: Try it yourself

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Use the exact legal terms: 'satisfactory quality', 'fit for purpose', 'as described' When evaluating consumer rights, consider whether citizens actually know and use their rights Link consumer rights to broader citizenship themes like accountability and fairness
